clue.text: Poet Laureate departs still sharp

indicators.note: whatever departs leaves the word, so those letters are taken away from the other piece

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation of the title Poet Laureate
still and calm, as a lake on a windless day

explanation.surface: A national poet stalks off, still smarting and cutting in his remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PL from PLACID to leave ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective describes a tart taste or a cutting tone, both senses of sharp.

clue.text: Skilled worker periodically saw Ruth in Spain

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular gaps, so only every other letter of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: the even letters of the three-word phrase, starting with its second

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker reports spotting a woman called Ruth on a trip to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsman, a person trained in a manual trade such as carpentry or weaving.

clue.text: Tack will get upset after tax is taken dishonestly

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting something tips it over so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: Tack is the setter, so the setter will becomes I'll, apostrophe dropped
as in I get it meaning I have got it, understood
pay after tax is net pay

explanation.surface: The setter grumbles about losing money to the taxman, claiming it was taken from him dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL + GOT + NET turned up to TEN. Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, here Tack, for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten goods or gains are those acquired by illegal or unfair means, such as theft or fraud.

clue.text: Expert charging less created issue

indicators.note: to charge a gun is to load it, so the second piece is loaded with the first

explanation.surface: A specialist who cut their fees caused a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The expert sits inside after the first two letters. Issue here means offspring, not a problem or a magazine number.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce is to breed, and issue is an old legal word for children or descendants.

clue.text: Showing flexibility, not starting and stopping

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone is flexible but stalls, neither starting nor stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a thing is bringing it to a halt, so ending and stopping are synonyms as verb forms.

clue.text: Not having to make payment spared tears?

blocks.note: rents are rips, as in cloth

explanation.surface: A tenant let off the rent is spared tears of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the last two words as a rip that has been released: RENT then FREE. Tears looks like weeping but means rips.
explanation.definitionFit: Living rent-free means occupying a place without paying the landlord, so no payment is required.

clue.text: Contrarian was up and down about dividing X

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
something dividing another sits in the middle of it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: an X on a ballot paper is a vote

explanation.surface: An awkward character fluctuated in mood over some unknown X.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like an unknown quantity, but it is the cross a voter marks on a ballot paper. Was up and down reads as mood swings but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil's advocate argues the opposite case for argument's sake, which is exactly what a contrarian does.

clue.text: Hide money for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is given as it would be heard

explanation.surface: Someone conceals funds from the accountants who check the books.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors looks like accountants, but here it means people who hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, a hiding place for valuables or supplies, so hide works as a noun.

clue.text: Idle South American stopped working outside

indicators.note: the last piece goes outside, wrapping round the others

explanation.surface: A South American worker downs tools and stands idle.
explanation.walkthrough: South American looks like one idea, a person from that continent, but it splits into two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused is no longer in service, lying idle in the sense of unused machinery or buildings.

clue.text: Folks imagine a new motorway going ahead that will ease congestion

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them
going ahead places this piece at the front of the rest

explanation.surface: People picture a new motorway being built to relieve traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: The congestion is not road traffic but a blocked or upset gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk of magnesia is a laxative and antacid remedy, easing a congested bowel or stomach.

clue.text: Hard to believe that is 500 squared

explanation.surface: Someone finds it incredible that 500 multiplied by itself comes to some figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Squared looks like a sum, but it means matched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that tally agree, and accounts that are squared have been brought into agreement or settled.

clue.text: Young nuns and what they should have?

blocks.note: first meaning: nuns still in training before taking vows
second meaning, split in two words: an absence of any bad habits

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, NO VICES, for the second meaning. The question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are probationers in a religious order, and a woman training to be a nun is one.

clue.text: Odd gifts relative left in sock?

definitions.text: Odd gifts relative left in sock?

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A quirky aunt or uncle stuffs strange presents into a sock.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: odd small gifts left by family in a Christmas sock. Odd here means miscellaneous as well as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking fillers are cheap small presents placed in a hanging Christmas stocking, often from family members.

clue.text: Held back by extremely fit one-armed brief

indicators.note: letters held by the words are gripped inside them, waiting to be read out
going back means the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the run straddling the three words

explanation.surface: An athlete who has lost an arm is held back despite being very fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of extremely to the start of one; read backwards they give NOTIFY. Brief is the verb, as in briefing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to give them information or instructions, which is to notify them.

clue.text: Fell over

indicators.note: over can mean once more, as in starting a task over, which sits in front of the verb

blocks.note: slipped, as into a bad habit

explanation.walkthrough: Over can mean again, as in do it over, so this is falling a second time rather than tumbling to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a former illness or habit after an improvement.

clue.text: This chap is too disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone points to a man and declares him mentally unbalanced.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: rearrange the letters and the result describes such a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociopath has a personality disorder marked by antisocial behaviour, a man disturbed in mind.

clue.text: Tory resorted to drinking with uplifting female figure

indicators.note: re-sorted means put in order again, so those letters are rearranged
a word drinking another takes it inside, swallowing it
in a down entry, lifting a piece up moves it to the top of the column

explanation.surface: A Conservative takes to drink alongside an inspiring woman.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes to the top, then TORY rearranged, then TO holding W. Resorted reads as re-sorted, not went to a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-two is a number, and a figure is a numeral or number.

clue.text: Home depressed after sex party stopped halfway

indicators.note: stopping halfway means only the first half of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: the name given to the parties of Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi

explanation.surface: Someone stays at home feeling down after an orgy was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunga bunga was the tabloid name for the notorious parties of Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi; only half the phrase is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a type of home.

clue.text: Hold her bag and uniform tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep a firm grip on a woman's bag and uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight looks like an instruction to grip firmly, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, crushing embrace, and a hold is a grip in wrestling or embracing.

clue.text: See overcharge during meal withdrawn as one's bill turns up

indicators.note: something happening during a thing falls inside it, so the first pieces go within
withdrawn means pulled back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: short for vide, Latin for see
o/c is the commercial abbreviation for overcharge

explanation.surface: A diner spots that they have been overcharged for a meal when the bill arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill is a beak, not a restaurant tab, and the definition describes the bird by its upturned beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird famous for its long slender beak that curves upwards at the tip.

clue.text: Cheats admit offence

blocks.note: as a school takes or admits pupils

explanation.surface: A swindler confesses to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Admit offence reads as a phrase, but it splits into two pieces read side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to deceive or fool them, which is what a cheat does.

clue.text: I see American statesman's wife leaving for another

indicators.note: the wife leaving means that letter walks out of the word

blocks.note: a man from an American state, Iowa

explanation.surface: A politician's wife walks out on him for another man.
explanation.walkthrough: Statesman is read as state's man: an Iowan. Remove W and add OH in front. Another means another American state's man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Ohio is also a man of an American state, so he is another such state-dweller beside the Iowan.

clue.text: This could make someone like me seethe in a hurry

blocks.clueFragment: This could make someone like me seethe
blocks.note: surface reading: something that would infuriate the setter
setter's reading: a crossword setter racing a deadline is under time pressure and gets cross

explanation.walkthrough: Someone like me is the setter, Tack; solvers racing to finish fast would irritate a setter who wants the puzzle savoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Working against the clock means racing to finish before time runs out, so rushed or hurried.

clue.text: In Canada ptarmigans change with conditions

indicators.note: the answer is in the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Canadian ptarmigans turn white in winter to suit the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The ptarmigan, a grouse, really does moult into white plumage for snow, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to adjust to new circumstances, altering to fit a changed environment.

clue.text: Phones the man a day ahead of schedule

indicators.note: ahead of places what comes before in front of the next piece

blocks.note: to set a time is to schedule it

explanation.surface: A man rings someone a day earlier than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: Phones is a noun here, the headphones, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, often with a microphone, and phones is a casual word for headphones.

clue.text: Public covers costs

blocks.note: as a secret that is out is public
as a cloth lays over a table

explanation.surface: A public body pays for its expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: Covers is a verb, as in laying a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlays are sums spent, expenditure on something, so they are costs.

clue.text: Becomes known for arranging great sound

indicators.note: arranging puts letters into a new order, as a musician arranges a piece

explanation.surface: A musician makes a name by producing a fine sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Arranging and sound point to music, but arranging is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: News or a rumour that gets around spreads widely, so it comes to be widely heard of.

clue.text: Polish barman, ignoring procedure, makes punch

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the Polish composer, a man whose music is written in bars
short for operation, a surgical procedure

explanation.surface: A bartender from Poland skips the formalities and mixes a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Barman looks like a bartender but means a composer of bars of music. Polish could also be the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To chin someone is British slang for punching them on the jaw.
